en: Photograph the house number or address marker first, so every photo after it is tied to this property.
es: Fotografíe primero el número de la casa o el letrero de la dirección, para que todas las fotos después queden ligadas a esta propiedad.
why: Adjusters and your own records need every photo tied to an address without extra notes - a roofing trade-press source names this as the difference between a photo that proves something and one that gets ignored.

en: Check that your phone's location (GPS) is turned on before you start, so each photo's metadata records where it was taken.
es: Antes de empezar, confirme que la ubicación (GPS) de su teléfono esté activada, para que los metadatos de cada foto registren dónde se tomó.
why: Photo metadata (EXIF) records date, time and location automatically on most phones - your built-in proof of when and where, but only if location is turned on.

en: Wide shot of the front elevation, roofline to ground, showing the whole side of the house.
es: Foto amplia de la fachada frontal, desde el techo hasta el suelo, mostrando todo ese lado de la casa.
why: Adjuster training splits every inspection into front/left/rear/right elevations - a wide shot of each proves which side you mean before you zoom into damage.

en: Wide shot of the right elevation.
es: Foto amplia del lado derecho de la casa.
why: Same elevation-by-elevation standard as the front - lets anyone match a damage photo back to a specific wall later.

en: Wide shot of the rear elevation.
es: Foto amplia de la parte de atrás de la casa.
why: Completes the four-sides record - the rear is often the side homeowners forget to mention damage on.

en: Wide shot of the left elevation.
es: Foto amplia del lado izquierdo de la casa.
why: Completes all four elevations before any close-up photos are taken.

en: Photo an untouched side of the house next to the damaged (storm) side, for comparison.
es: Fotografíe un lado de la casa sin daño junto al lado dañado (lado de la tormenta), para comparar.
why: A clean side next to the damaged side shows the difference is from the storm, not wear - adjusters look for that contrast.

en: Photo window screens and the AC unit's fins for dents or tears - they show hail size and which direction it hit from.
es: Fotografíe las mallas de las ventanas y las aletas del aire acondicionado buscando abolladuras o rasgaduras - muestran el tamaño del granizo y de qué dirección pegó.
why: Soft aluminum fins dent easily and keep the dent shape, unlike siding or shingles - a reliable hail-direction indicator.

en: Close-up photos of soft metals - roof vents, flashing, gutter straps, gutter aprons - showing any dents.
es: Fotos de cerca de los metales blandos - ventilas del techo, tapajuntas, soportes de la canaleta - mostrando cualquier abolladura.
why: Soft metal dents are one of the clearest, least-arguable signs of hail size, and one of the first things adjusters check.

en: Photo the gutters and downspouts for dings, and look inside the gutter for loose granules.
es: Fotografíe las canaletas y bajantes buscando golpes, y revise adentro de la canaleta si hay gránulos sueltos.
why: Granules knocked loose by hail collect in the gutter - a photo of them backs up what you found on the roof.

en: Wide photo of the storm-facing side of the siding, then move closer.
es: Foto amplia del lado del siding que dio hacia la tormenta, luego acérquese.
why: Vinyl cracks/chips and fiber-cement dents show most on the side the wind-driven hail actually hit.

en: Close-up of each hit on the siding with a coin or tape measure next to it for scale.
es: Foto de cerca de cada golpe en el siding, con una moneda o cinta métrica al lado para mostrar el tamaño.
why: A close-up with no size reference is easy to dismiss - a coin or tape measure proves how big the hit really is.

en: Before climbing, take a wide photo of each roof slope from the ground, naming which direction it faces.
es: Antes de subir, tome una foto amplia de cada agua del techo desde el suelo, diciendo hacia qué dirección da.
why: Labeling each slope (north/south/east/west) before you climb means every later close-up can be matched to the right part of the roof.

en: If the roof is wet, icy, steep or otherwise unsafe to climb, take ground-level photos of the roofline and edges from multiple angles instead of skipping documentation entirely.
es: Si el techo está mojado, con hielo, muy inclinado o no es seguro para subir, tome fotos desde el suelo del borde del techo desde varios ángulos, en lugar de no documentar nada.
why: Ground-level smartphone photos from the right angles can still document a roof's condition when climbing isn't safe - a real fallback, not just 'skip it'.

en: Mark a 10x10 ft test square on one slope (away from trees/vents) with tape or flags - not chalk - and photograph it wide, showing the whole square.
es: Marque un cuadro de prueba de 10x10 pies en un agua (lejos de árboles/ventilas) con cinta o banderines - no con gis - y fotografíelo completo.
why: InterNACHI warns that chalk-circling hits can make damage look bigger than it is; tape or flags mark the square without changing what the photo actually shows.

en: Medium shot of the test square showing the hits you counted.
es: Foto a media distancia del cuadro de prueba mostrando los golpes que contó.
why: A medium shot bridges the wide slope photo and the close-up, so the hit count is traceable back to the exact square.

en: Close-up of one hit inside the square with a coin or tape measure for scale.
es: Foto de cerca de un golpe dentro del cuadro con una moneda o cinta métrica para mostrar el tamaño.
why: Same scale-reference rule as siding - a close-up hit photo with nothing next to it for size is the easiest kind of photo for an adjuster to wave off.

en: Repeat one test square (wide, medium, close-up) on every slope you can safely reach - most insurers look for hits on 2 or more slopes.
es: Repita un cuadro de prueba (amplio, medio, de cerca) en cada agua a la que pueda subir con seguridad - la mayoría de aseguradoras buscan golpes en 2 o más aguas.
why: One square on one slope is easy to call 'not enough'; the same pattern on multiple slopes is harder to argue with.

en: Photo any lifted, creased, or missing shingles, and any exposed nail heads.
es: Fotografíe tejas de asfalto levantadas, dobladas o faltantes, y cualquier clavo expuesto.
why: Wind damage shows differently than hail - creases, lifted edges and missing shingles are the tell, not round hits.

en: Photo any soffit, fascia, or siding panels that are loose, cracked, or blown off.
es: Fotografíe cualquier sofito, fascia o panel de siding que esté suelto, agrietado o volado.
why: Wind pulls panels loose at the edges first - a common wind-damage point adjusters check.

en: Photo any other storm damage nearby - dented mailbox, fence, shed roof, satellite dish, or a neighbor's damaged roof visible from the yard.
es: Fotografíe cualquier otro daño de la tormenta cerca - buzón abollado, cerca, techo del cobertizo, antena satelital, o el techo dañado de un vecino visible desde el patio.
why: Collateral damage on soft, unrelated objects backs up that a real storm hit this property, not just wear over time.

en: Photo the chimney flashing and cap for damage or gaps.
es: Fotografíe el tapajuntas y la tapa de la chimenea buscando daño o espacios abiertos.
why: Flashing is a common leak point after a storm and is easy to miss in a general roof photo.

en: Photo any skylights for cracks or hail hits on the frame.
es: Fotografíe cualquier tragaluz buscando grietas o golpes de granizo en el marco.
why: Skylights are a commonly overlooked damage and leak point.

en: If it helps, write down one already-known measurement (like the width of the front door) as a backup size reference, in case a close-up photo's coin or tape isn't clear later.
es: Si ayuda, anote una medida ya conocida (como el ancho de la puerta principal) como referencia extra de tamaño, en caso de que la moneda o cinta en una foto de cerca no se vea clara después.
why: A backup reference measurement is a simple way to double-check scale later if a close-up photo's coin or tape measure isn't clear.

en: Before you leave, show the homeowner the photos on your phone and explain what each one means.
es: Antes de irse, muéstrele al dueño de casa las fotos en su teléfono y explíquele qué significa cada una.
why: Reps who walk the homeowner through the evidence at the door build trust and close faster than reps who just take pictures and talk about it later.

en: After the job is done, take the same elevation photos again to make a before/after pair.
es: Cuando termine el trabajo, tome las mismas fotos de las fachadas otra vez para tener un par de antes y después.
why: Before/after pairs are what wins the next kitchen table and what HMP can use for referrals and reviews.
